Private Kartchner Caverns Tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Kartchner Caverns tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale as one vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 9-hour day: the group is driven to the park, waited on while you take the cave tour you reserved with Arizona State Parks, then driven home. Choosing between the two cave tours: the Rotunda/Throne tour runs all year and is built around how the cave was made, while the Big Room tour is the seasonal formations-and-fauna tour — both in the park's own words below. The published window is 8-9 hours and it bills 8 hours, so the day starts at $1,000 and the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,160 before 8% tax. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 18, 2026

Which Kartchner Caverns cave tour is better, the Big Room or the Rotunda/Throne Room?

Neither is better in the abstract. They are different rooms with different subjects, and only one runs all year: Arizona State Parks lists the Rotunda/Throne tour without a season and publishes a seasonal window for the Big Room tour. The 9-hour private day below is built around whichever check-in you are given. The park's own descriptions choose for you. The Rotunda/Throne tour is framed around how the cave was made: "Discover the role that water plays in creating the caverns." On it you pass the discoverers' original trail, delicate formations and "Kubla Khan," which the park calls the largest column formation in Arizona. For a single tour, or a visit outside the Big Room's season, this is the one. The Big Room tour is framed around the life and colour of the cave rather than its plumbing: "Marvel at the many strange and colorful formations." and "Learn about the cave fauna, both living and ancient." It suits a group that has already walked the Rotunda and Throne Room, or came for the formations rather than the discovery story. Two rules are the park's, not ours. Arizona State Parks states that "video or photography is not permitted inside the cave, with your cell phone or a camera." And tour length, walking conditions, accessibility and age rules differ by tour. Both official pages are cited below; nothing about the cave's own cost or timetable is repeated here.

What is a private Kartchner Caverns tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale?

It is the whole vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 9-hour day to the park and back, not a seat on somebody else's coach. 6 vehicles are offered for it, from 6 to 29 seats, and priced from $1,000 to $2,360, every figure quoted in writing first. Scottsdale Sprinters sells the transport around your cave booking, never the cave tour itself. Your group decides who is aboard and how the hours are spent; the chauffeur drives, waits while you are underground, and drives home — off one check-in time, not a departure somebody else chose. Per head the arithmetic is plainer than it looks. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter splits $1,160 across its seats, about $83 each; the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) splits $1,800 across 29, about $62. Those are the current published hourly rates carried across this day, never a fare per person, and park admission is separate.

How does the private day work, from pickup to the drive home?

The tour publishes 8 steps and states the day as 8-9 hours, and every one of them hangs off a single fixed point: the check-in time on the cave booking you already hold. The second and third steps name it outright. "Confirmed cave tour at the reserved check-in time" is the only step with a time attached, so "Morning pickup" is set backward from it. Everything after the cave is time the vehicle is already paid for, which is why the last stop is optional. The row also publishes what the day is meant to show: Kartchner Caverns State Park, Confirmed cave tour selected by the group, Living cave formations, Hummingbird garden, Benson historic town, Desert scenery. That list is the whole brief. Which vehicle fits the group, and what does the day cost?

Group size decides it. This tour offers 6 vehicles, and every row below prices the identical 9-hour day: the published hourly rate times 8 billable hours, because 9 requested hours earn 1 free hour on the standard ladder, against each vehicle's own 4-hour minimum. Up to 6 travellers the Luxury SUV (Suburban) runs the day for $1,000; the Executive Black Sprinter and Executive White Sprinter share a rate at $145 an hour; the Maybach Jet Sprinter leads the row's own list. Past 14 seats it is the Mini Bus (24 Pax) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). The per-seat column divides the day total by seated capacity — friends splitting one fare. The Luxury SUV (Suburban) is the least expensive day at $1,000; the Mini Bus (24 Pax) the least expensive seat at $62. What is in the fare, and what is not?

A 9-hour day in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,160 before 8% tax — $145 an hour across 8 billable hours, roughly $83 a seat split 14 ways. The least expensive vehicle on the list runs the same day for $1,000. Three rules build every number: the day is priced by the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, hours above the ladder's rungs earn free hours, and 8% tax is the only addition. Nothing is by the mile or per passenger. 50% is taken today by card, the balance 48 hours before pickup. What the fare excludes is the part of the day that is not ours to sell: "Arizona State Parks describes Kartchner as a living cave protected through specific visitor rules. Review the park's current cave history and conservation guidance directly; transportation does not include park admission or interpretation." Lunch is a stop rather than a service for the same reason — "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop."

Who books a private day at the caverns?

Groups — and that is deliberately as far as this page will go. The tour row names no audience — no school, no club, no company — so the only honest description is the shape of the booking: one vehicle, one chauffeur, 9 hours, and a party between 6 and 29 people. What the booking is good at follows from that shape, not from a customer list. Everyone arrives at the same check-in together, which matters when the park has given the group one reserved time. Bags and coats stay aboard, and the vehicle is waiting when the tour comes back up. Group size is the one real constraint: past 29 seats the party moves as more than one vehicle, quoted together.

Can we combine the caverns with Tombstone and Bisbee?

Ask for it as a written quote rather than as a bolt-on. Tombstone and Bisbee is published here as its own day tour with its own window, and nothing on this page combines the two: the 9-hour caverns day is priced as the row publishes it, and no combined itinerary exists to print. The reason to ask rather than assume is the fixed point again: the cave check-in cannot move, and a second destination comes straight out of the hours around it. Send the date, the headcount, the check-in and the stops you want. If the caverns are the reason for the trip, keep this day for them and book the other tour separately. What should we bring, and what stays in the vehicle?

Bring what a day partly underground and partly outdoors needs, and leave the rest aboard. Across the 9-hour window the cabin is the group's locker: coats, bags and camera kit sit in it while the group is underground, and the chauffeur is there with them. Beyond that, conditions belong to the park, and the row's own answer is the right one: "Tour length, walking conditions, lighting, accessibility, age rules, and health considerations are controlled by Arizona State Parks and can vary by tour. Review the current official guidance and contact the park with accessibility or health questions before reserving." Inside the vehicle the chauffeur is a resource rather than a fixture: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

Where can the day start, and how is it quoted?

Pickup is a street address in any of the 10 metro cities with a published service-area page, not a zone or a depot. Reserving takes 3 things — the date, the number of people and one address — plus the cave check-in as soon as you have it. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. One pickup address for the whole party keeps a group together. Every figure here is today's published table; the quote you act on is the written one, naming the vehicle, the hours, the 8% tax and the 50% deposit, confirmed before anything is charged. Call Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339, or send those 3 things and request a current quote.
